newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady, whipsawed by crude oil.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady, whipsawed by crude oil.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady on Friday in quiet trading, digesting this week's gains after being whipsawed by crude and heavy buying interest in swaps.
But the market was balanced to slightly oversupplied heading into the second half of November, traders said.
Four big Skikda cargoes of 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes each were expected this month, with one already loaded, and a few smaller ones, one trader said.
A 51,000 tonne clean tanker was fixed out of the west Med for the U.S. Atlantic Coast loading Nov 20, tanker sources said.
An Alexandria cargo loaded this week and one to two more were expected next week, a trader said.
He said the market will be closely watching weather conditions at Skikda next week for loading delays.
"There is quite good supply and I don't see the demand in Northwest Europe," he said.
But other traders said naphtha could still be dragged reluctantly higher if crude rallies next week.
"I think it's crude-driven," a broker said.
Nov swaps ended unchanged at $226/$227 and Dec rose about $1 to $221/$222.
Cargoes were notionally valued at $225/$227 cif.
